That behavior is right. I clicked the box-shaped control on "Designing Better Design Systems" and it left my main collection, then over in the Archive view there it was, with the count showing 1. So archiving tucks something out of my everyday list without throwing it away — which is exactly the "keep it but get it out of sight" thing I was missing before. And I can see there's a "Restore" button on it, so putting it back is easy, which reassures me it's reversible.

Two things I want to be sure of before I call archiving done:

- When something's archived, I don't just want it hidden from All bookmarks — I'd also expect it to stay out of my normal search results, so old stuff I've deliberately tucked away doesn't keep resurfacing when I search. It should only turn up when I'm actually looking in the Archive. Does it work that way?
- And I want to be clear that this is different from deleting. Archiving is the reversible "hide it" — but I'd also want a real delete for things I want gone for good, and I'd expect that one to actually remove the bookmark permanently, not just tuck it away. Is there a separate delete, and does it truly remove the item?
